final_answer: Ice floats on water due to the unique arrangement of its structure, which is influenced by hydrogen bonding. In liquid water, the structure is more fluid, allowing the components to move closer together. However, when water freezes, hydrogen bonds form a stable, open hexagonal lattice. This lattice creates more space between the components compared to the liquid state, resulting in a lower density. Since density determines buoyancy, the lower density of the solid form allows it to float on the denser liquid. This phenomenon is a key reason why bodies of water can support life even in freezing conditions.
